searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's, two left unspent. Five were restricted by domain: elgrifo.com once (the families, the vines), losbermejos.com with the importer once (the range), the DO La Palma's vinoslapalma.com once (the lease of 1555), boe.es once (the two orders), each read as primary through its summary where the domain is the body's own, and the importer's José Pastor and Indigo domains once for the Benje sheets. The two shared searches are the parentage of Malvasía Volcánica (El Grifo and Los Bermejos) and the BOE's orders of 1994 and 1995 (Envínate and Suertes del Marqués). The per record counts above give the shared searches once each: El Grifo 7, Los Bermejos 3, Suertes del Marqués 4 with the Real Academia, Envínate 4, Teneguía 6. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites and their heights, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

tested: 1775, the builder and the claim of the oldest winery, with the house's history read through search: the covered press house of 1775 by its founding inscription, built by the Beneficiado of the parish church of Teguise, by Vinetur, Vozpópuli and the house; the oldest winery of the Canaries and among the ten oldest of Spain stands as the house's claim and is hedged so. Borne out.

The families: the house's history page names three families (the founder's, the De Castro from about 1820 and, from the 1880s, the descendants of the buyer of that time), with first labels in 1935 and El Grifo S.A. formed in 1980. The author's "passed through three families since" counted one family too many. Changed.

The vines: forty to sixty years on Vinissimus and on the author's reading of the house's sheets, forty to fifty on the house's shop page for 2023; ungrafted and pre phylloxera on the house's vineyard page. The record's forty to sixty years by the house's account stands, with the shop's narrower figure open.

The making: no sheet of the Seco giving the 16 degrees, the cloudy, unfiltered holding or the day's chilling was found in two searches; the house's own yeast is borne out on its Lías sheet of 2022, and the hand harvest into small crates at the end of July on the sheets of the Semidulce, which the house says is made together with the Seco. The unconfirmed details are cut. Changed.

Lías: the house's page and Kysela's sheet give about seven months on lees kept in suspension, stirred, with 30 per cent in 500 litre French oak and the rest in tank, not a year in tank. Changed in others and ageing.

César Manrique: the griffin he drew for the house is borne out by the house and Gazette Life; the museum on his advice by the house, the Lanzarote Guidebook (1981 for his urging) and the house's history (works from 1986, the last stages in 1990 and 1991). No year for the logo was found in two searches, so "since 1990" is cut. His dates (1919 to 1992) rest on the Fundación's biography, which the author cites, and were not searched again.

Malvasía Volcánica as a natural crossing of Malvasía Aromática and Marmajuelo: Wein.plus (DNA analysis of 2009) and the SSR study in Horticulturae (Malvasia Dubrovacka, the aromatic Malvasía of Spain, by Bermejuela, which is Marmajuelo). Borne out. The glass (orange blossom, jasmine, apricot, saline) on Decantalo's notes of three vintages. Borne out. Serving at 8 to 10 degrees sits inside the house's own 7 to 10.
The questions: one key each, distractors plausible, explanations teach. The house rules: nobody living named, no price, no score, British, no dash.

changed.was: By the house's own sheet, the grapes are picked from late July as each part of the island ripens and chilled for a day; the must is then settled and fermented with a yeast selected from the estate's own vineyards. After fermentation the wine is held slightly cloudy and unfiltered at 16 degrees Celsius until bottling, to keep the perfume of the grape.
changed.now: By the house's own sheets, the grapes are picked by hand into small crates from late July, as each part of the island ripens, and the must is settled and fermented with the house's own yeast, selected from its vineyards. The wine is bottled young, to keep the perfume of the grape.
changed.why: Two searches found no sheet of the Seco with the 16 degrees, the cloudy holding or the chilling; the house's own yeast and the settling stand on its Lías sheet of 2022, and the hand harvest at the end of July on its Semidulce sheets, made together with the Seco.

The Brut Nature's figure is changed to what both bear; the sweet note stands.

The flagship: Spanish Wine Lover names Bermejo Malvasía Seco the house's star wine, the larger part of its production (a volatile figure, kept out). The glass (ripe lemon and mango, a hint of wildflowers) on Decantalo and the author's Flatiron note. Borne out.
The label: Spanish merchants and Spanish Wine Lover print Bermejo Malvasía Seco, the American importer Los Bermejos Malvasía Volcánica Seco; no photograph of the label was read. Open.

The plots and the heights: about twenty on the house's sheet of 2021 as the author read it, twenty five on Bodeboca, thirty five with vines of ten to 180 years and heights of 250 to 800 metres on Clos des Millésimes. A single figure of twenty taught a vintage's number as the wine's; now many plots, about twenty on the sheet of 2021. Changed in sites, table, story, label and trap.

The making: each plot apart in small concrete and steel vats (a merchant), 60 per cent in concrete and 40 in French oak for eight months on another vintage, about a fifth in 500 litre demi muids for 2016, 500 litre and 2,000 to 4,500 litre casks for the house's wines generally. The eleven months in foudre and barrel was one vintage's; now eight to eleven months, partly in concrete. Changed.

Suertes: no source in one search explained the name; the Real Academia's historical dictionary defines suerte as a small rural plot, above all one received by inheritance. The record's "the old word for the small plots into which the valley's land was divided" claimed more than any source read. Changed in story and card.
The DO: the BOE (BOE-A-1995-25944) gives the order of 15 November 1995 ratifying the rules approved by the Canary government's order of 29 December 1994. The story now says both. Changed.

The making, on the importer's sheets of several vintages: each parcel apart in concrete tanks and small open tubs, ten to twenty days with a daily punching down, pressed into old French barriques for the malolactic, eight months on the fine lees in the same barrels, no bâtonnage, bottled unfiltered. Whole bunches appear only on the sheet of 2020 (about half), which also gives 300 metres; the other sheets describe destemmed fruit. Whole bunches are cut. Changed.
The site: Santiago del Teide at 900 to 1,000 metres (one listing) or about 1,000 (others); old, ungrafted Listán Prieto. Borne out.
The blend: 95 Listán Prieto and 5 Tintilla on one listing; the 2024 about 90 Listán Prieto, 9 Listán Blanco and 1 Tintilla (Flask). The touch of Listán Blanco is now some. Changed.

Borne out; the source now cites the BOE's summary page, since the author's PDF range could not be matched in the results.

tested: The founding: 1947 on Lonely Planet and a guide, 1945 on Spanish Wine Lover and Guía Repsol (for the building). Founded stays empty and the story's 1945 and 1947 stand. Llanovid as the co-operative and Teneguía as its brand: Spanish Wine Lover and a review listing (Llanovid S. C. L. Bodegas Teneguía). Borne out.

The lease of 27 September 1555 for a vineyard of Malvasía, in the protocols of a notary of the island: the DO La Palma's own paper. Fuencaliente's share of the island's Malvasía (about 95 per cent by the DO's page) bears out "most". Borne out.

The sweet wine's rule: the DO's pliego defines Malvasía dulce as made from overripe grapes of the variety by the island's traditional methods, picking late; the pliego of 2011 sets at least 45 grams of sugar for sweet wines, and the Canary rules of 2003 said more than 45. Now at least 45. Changed.

The eruption: 26 October to 18 November 1971 by RTVC and the petrology paper; the Roque de Teneguía ringed by lavas of the Fuencaliente eruption of 1677 (Hispanopedia) and the 1971 vents near those of 1677 (the paper). Borne out, and the story question's explanation stands.
The subzones: the ministry's certificate and the DO's own report give three, Fuencaliente, Hoyo de Mazo and the north. Borne out.

The glass: no note of this bottling was found in one search; the notes given (honey, candied apricot, beeswax) are those of La Palma's sweet Malvasía from another maker. The glass now says so, and orange peel, on no source read, is cut. Changed.

The members: about 300 growers across the three subzones on Spanish Wine Lover alone, a volatile figure; the story's sentence that the members come from across La Palma is cut. Llanos Negros: the co-operative's website carries the name and the DO's list (the author's reading) gives it as a brand; the second brand and the place name were on no source read. Changed.

The table's "the old sweet Canary in a modern bottle" said more than the history bears; now an heir to the sweet Canary of history, as the region record has it. The house rules: the winemaker is not named, no price, no score, British, no dash.

livingNote: None of these is named in the fragment's prose; the read together agent adds those it judges living to people.json. Jancis Robinson and James Suckling, met in the results, are already in people.json and cited nowhere; a Master of Wine's newsletter under his own name was met and cited nowhere. Described, never named, for want of dates in two sources: the priest of Teguise who built the press house of 1775 (Antonio de Torres Ribera, 1725 to 1807 on the house's page alone), his nephew and heir, the De Castro buyer of about 1820, the buyer of the 1880s (who died in 1912 by the house) and his daughter and son in law of the first labels of 1935. César Manrique (1919 to 1992) is dead and named with his dates on the Fundación César Manrique's biography, which the author cites; the refuter did not search them again.
swapNote: The author proposed no swap. The plan's note offered Los Bermejos's Listán Negro rosado as the alternative if the group needed the spread; the refuter refuses it: Spanish Wine Lover calls Bermejo Malvasía Seco the house's star wine and the larger part of what it makes, the American importer lists the Seco first, and the record keeps the two dry Malvasías apart (El Grifo's house yeast and Colección range, Los Bermejos's tank made Seco beside its oaked white), with each question testing a different point. The other four picks stand: El Grifo's Seco Colección, 7 Fuentes as Suertes del Marqués's village red, Benje Tinto as Envínate's Tenerife red, and Teneguía's sweet Malvasía Aromática, said plainly to be a co-operative's.
planNotes: el-grifo: answered. 1775 rests on the house's founding inscription with Vinetur and Vozpópuli; the oldest winery of the Canaries and among the ten oldest of Spain are hedged as the house's claim; the vines ungrafted by the house and forty to sixty years by Vinissimus and the house's sheets (forty to fifty on its shop page, open); no living member of the family named.

los-bermejos: answered. Founded left empty: 2001 is a revival of an older estate by Gayot and the DO's page, a founding by Spanish Wine Lover; the label stays open; the rosado alternative refused (see the swap note); the owner not named.

suertes-del-marques: answered. The blend is Listán Negro with Tintilla on most listings and Castellana Negra on the house's sheet of 2021, both said; the DO Valle de la Orotava on the label by the listings; 2006 by the house's distributor and a retailer; Vidonia its Listán Blanco; nobody living named.

envinate: answered. 2005 by Grandi Bottiglie and Cru World Wine; Listán Prieto with Tintilla and some Listán Blanco; Santiago del Teide at about 1,000 metres; Benje Tinto under the DO Ycoden-Daute-Isora by Decanter's review and listings; the four founders not named; the record is about Tenerife, with Táganan, Lousas and Almansa named as the group's other places.

teneguia: answered. Llanovid the co-operative and Teneguía its brand on two accounts; founded left empty for 1945 and 1947; the label words stay open; Estelar left out on one guide; the record says it is a co-operative.

codexInTension.says: Fuencaliente's sweet Malvasía grows on the ash of the San Antonio eruption of 1677
codexInTension.read: The petrology paper on the 1971 eruption places the 1677 vents close to those of 1971 near Fuencaliente, and Hispanopedia calls the lavas round the Roque de Teneguía those of the Fuencaliente eruption of 1677; the author read the DO La Palma's page as calling the San Antonio volcano itself prehispanic. The refuter did not read San Antonio's own age, so the tension is reported as plausible, not settled: the record says only an older eruption of 1677.

codexInTension.read: Wein.plus (DNA analysis of 2009) and the SSR study in Horticulturae give Malvasía Volcánica as a natural crossing of the aromatic Malvasía of Spain and Marmajuelo (Bermejuela), which is what the region record and the fragment say; the Codex is not in tension, and the house's clone is not taught.
